![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/4b7c8c679171c1dcb6ef44b33696ba2ccce87b3f690643af979476d8dfb285ce.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+3b$, find $\lambda .$
worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+3b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $3b.$ So, we first draw the vector $3b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/f67af4512a7ab61f862932a60dafc25ef62bc46335b7d7df323fe889f8728e6b.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $3b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=\frac{1}{2}|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=\frac{1}{2}a.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =3b+\frac{1}{2}a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+3b=\frac{1}{2}a+3b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =\frac{1}{2}
$$
